# Bundled packs

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-pack-docs.ts. Run `pnpm docs:packs` after changing a pack. -->

Each pack below ships with plughive. A pack that needs a key loads without
one; its tools return a missing-key error until you save the key in the
dashboard. The core tools (search_tools, list_artifacts, ...) are described
in [protocol.md](protocol.md).

## brave

**Brave Search**, version 0.1.0.

Web search through the Brave Search API with your own key (search_web).

Keys:

- `BRAVE_API_KEY`: Brave Search API key. Get one at https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/app/keys

Permissions:

- Network: `api.search.brave.com`

## browser

**Cloud browsers (Browserbase, Steel)**, version 0.1.0.

Start and close Browserbase and Steel cloud browser sessions, fetch pages, and navigate and screenshot with Steel into the library.

Keys:

- `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` (optional): Browserbase API key. Get one at https://www.browserbase.com/settings
- `STEEL_API_KEY` (optional): Steel API key. Get one at https://app.steel.dev/settings/api-keys

Permissions:

- Network: `api.browserbase.com`, `api.steel.dev`
- Artifact library: write

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `browserbase_close_session` | End a Browserbase session so it stops billing. |
| `browserbase_create_session` | Start a Browserbase cloud browser session (billed per minute until closed or timed out). |
| `browserbase_fetch` | Fetch a web page through Browserbase's Fetch API (no session needed) and return its content as markdown, raw HTML or JSON (capped at 200k characters). |
| `browserbase_get_session` | Status of a Browserbase session (RUNNING, COMPLETED, ERROR, TIMED_OUT) with its live view URL while it runs. |
| `steel_create_session` | Start a Steel cloud browser session (billed per minute until released or timed out). |
| `steel_navigate` | Open a URL in a running Steel session and wait for it to load. |
| `steel_release_session` | Release (end) a Steel session so it stops billing. |
| `steel_screenshot` | Take a PNG screenshot of the current page of a Steel session (after opening `url` when given) and save it to the artifact library. |

## calendar

**Calendar (Cal.com)**, version 0.1.0.

Cal.com scheduling: list event types, find free slots, and create and cancel bookings.

Keys:

- `CALCOM_API_KEY`: Cal.com API key. Get one at https://app.cal.com/settings/developer/api-keys

Permissions:

- Network: `api.cal.com`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `calcom_cancel_booking` | Cancel a Cal.com booking by its uid. |
| `calcom_create_booking` | Book a Cal.com event type at `start` (an ISO time, ideally one returned by calcom_get_availability) for an attendee. |
| `calcom_get_availability` | Free slots of a Cal.com event type between `start` and `end` (dates or ISO times), grouped by day in `time_zone`. |
| `calcom_list_event_types` | List the Cal.com event types of the account (or of `username`): id, title, slug, length in minutes and whether each is hidden. |

## cli-bridge

**Agent CLIs**, version 0.1.0.

Use the agent CLIs already installed and signed in on this computer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, opencode, Copilot): list them, ask one a question and get its answer back, or have Antigravity draw an image into the library. Each runs on your own subscription, in a scratch folder or a folder you allow, as a background job with a timeout.

Off by default. Switch it on in the dashboard under Packs.

Permissions:

- Runs programs: `agy`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `copilot`, `node`
- Artifact library: write

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ask_agent_cli` | Ask an installed agent CLI (claude, codex, gemini, agy, opencode, copilot) one question in non-interactive mode, using the account it is signed in with, and return its answer {text, usage?, session_id?}. |
| `generate_image_via_agy` | Generate an image with the Antigravity CLI's (agy) built-in image tool, using the Google account agy is signed in with, and save it to the artifact library. |
| `list_agent_clis` | List the agent CLIs this pack can drive (claude, codex, gemini, agy, opencode, copilot): whether each is installed on the daemon's PATH, its version, and whether it is signed in where the CLI itself reports that (claude, codex; null otherwise). |

## elevenlabs

**ElevenLabs**, version 0.1.0.

Text to speech, sound effects, music, dubbing, transcription and voice isolation through ElevenLabs with your own key.

Keys:

- `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`: ElevenLabs API key. Get one at https://elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys

Permissions:

- Network: `api.elevenlabs.io`, `storage.googleapis.com`
- Artifact library: full

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `elevenlabs_dub` | Dub a library audio or video artifact (up to 50 MB) into another language, keeping the speakers' voices. |
| `elevenlabs_get_dub` | Collect an earlier dubbing project by its id (for example after elevenlabs_dub timed out). |
| `elevenlabs_isolate_voice` | Remove background noise and music from a library audio or video artifact, keeping only the voice. |
| `elevenlabs_list_models` | List ElevenLabs speech models (cached 10 min) with language counts and text limits, plus this pack's defaults. |
| `elevenlabs_list_voices` | Search the voices available to this key. |
| `elevenlabs_music` | Compose music from a prompt (model music_v2_5), 3 to 600 seconds, optionally instrumental only. |
| `elevenlabs_sound_effect` | Generate a sound effect from a text description, 0.5 to 30 seconds. |
| `elevenlabs_text_to_speech` | Speak text with an ElevenLabs voice (default model eleven_multilingual_v2, up to 5000 characters). |
| `elevenlabs_transcribe` | Transcribe a library audio or video artifact (up to 50 MB) with Scribe. |
| `elevenlabs_usage` | Show the subscription tier, characters used and remaining, and when the quota resets. |

## fal

**fal.ai**, version 0.1.0.

Search and run fal.ai models (image, video, speech, music, transcription) with your own fal key. Outputs are saved to the library.

Keys:

- `FAL_KEY`: fal.ai API key. Get one at https://fal.ai/dashboard/keys

Permissions:

- Network: `api.fal.ai`, `queue.fal.run`, `fal.media`, `*.fal.media`
- Artifact library: full

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fal_describe_model` | Show a fal model's input JSON Schema, output fields, price and a ready-to-use fal_run call. |
| `fal_flux_dev` | Runs the fal model fal-ai/flux/dev (text-to-image). |
| `fal_get_result` | Collect the output of a fal job that was already submitted (for example after a timeout or a lost connection): {model, request_id}. |
| `fal_kling_video_v3_pro_image_to_video` | Runs the fal model fal-ai/kling-video/v3/pro/image-to-video (image-to-video). |
| `fal_minimax_speech_2_8_hd` | Runs the fal model fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-hd (text-to-speech). |
| `fal_nano_banana_pro` | Runs the fal model fal-ai/nano-banana-pro (text-to-image). |
| `fal_run` | Run any fal model through the queue: {model, input}. |
| `fal_search_models` | Search the fal.ai model catalog (1000+ image, video, audio, speech and 3D models). |
| `fal_train_lora` | Train a FLUX LoRA on fal (fal-ai/flux-lora-fast-training) from a zip of images: {images, trigger_word?, steps?, is_style?}. |

## finance-data

**Market data (Massive/Polygon and Alpha Vantage)**, version 0.1.0.

Read-only stock, crypto and forex prices: previous close and price bars from Massive (formerly Polygon.io), quotes and daily prices from Alpha Vantage. No trading.

Keys:

- `POLYGON_API_KEY` (optional): Massive (Polygon.io) API key. Get one at https://massive.com/dashboard/api-keys
- `ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY` (optional): Alpha Vantage API key. Get one at https://www.alphavantage.co/support/#api-key

Permissions:

- Network: `api.massive.com`, `www.alphavantage.co`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `alphavantage_daily` | Daily open, high, low, close and volume for a symbol from Alpha Vantage (TIME_SERIES_DAILY), newest first, up to `days` days (max 100). |
| `alphavantage_quote` | Latest price, change, volume and previous close for a symbol from Alpha Vantage (GLOBAL_QUOTE). |
| `polygon_aggregates` | Price bars (OHLCV) for a ticker over a date range from Massive (formerly Polygon.io), e.g. |
| `polygon_previous_close` | Previous trading day's open, high, low, close and volume for a ticker from Massive (formerly Polygon.io). |

## growth

**Growth**, version 0.1.0.

Find leads with a lead provider, keep them in a local store, score them against an ICP and draft cold email.

Keys:

- `APOLLO_API_KEY` (optional): Apollo API key. Get one at https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key

Permissions:

- Network: `api.apollo.io`
- Artifact library: write
- Calls the configured chat model
- Calls other tools: `firecrawl_scrape`, `dub_shorten_url`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `apollo_bulk_enrich_people` | Deprecated alias of enrich_people (provider fixed to apollo). |
| `apollo_enrich_company` | Deprecated alias of enrich_company (provider fixed to apollo). |
| `apollo_enrich_person` | Deprecated alias of enrich_person (provider fixed to apollo). |
| `apollo_health_check` | Deprecated alias of leads_provider_status (provider fixed to apollo). |
| `apollo_search_companies` | Deprecated alias of find_companies (provider fixed to apollo). |
| `apollo_search_people` | Deprecated alias of find_people (provider fixed to apollo). |
| `craft_icp` | Convert a product description into a structured ICP (titles, seniorities, employee_ranges, locations, keywords) ready to feed find_people. |
| `draft_cold_email` | Draft a 3-touch cold email sequence for a person. |
| `enrich_company` | Enrich a company by domain with a lead provider. |
| `enrich_people` | Bulk person enrichment with a lead provider. |
| `enrich_person` | Enrich one person with a lead provider. |
| `find_companies` | Search companies with a lead provider. |
| `find_people` | Search people with a lead provider (default: the first configured; currently Apollo). |
| `get_sender_profile` | Return the saved sender profile, or { exists: false } if none is set. |
| `leads_provider_status` | Which lead providers exist and which have an API key set. |
| `list_drafts` | List recent cold-email drafts (from draft_cold_email and personalize_outreach) joined to their lead and company rows. |
| `mark_contacted` | Update a person's contact_status (new\|drafted\|sent\|replied\|won\|lost\|skipped). |
| `personalize_outreach` | Draft a 3-touch cold email sequence grounded in the prospect's website. |
| `pipeline_run` | End-to-end client-finding pipeline: craft_icp, find_people, score_lead, research_prospect (unique companies), draft_cold_email (top scored). |
| `query_companies` | Local filter against the lead store's companies (no API call). |
| `query_leads` | Local query against the lead store (no API call). |
| `research_prospect` | Generate a markdown research brief for a company (auto-enriches through the lead provider if the company is not stored). |
| `score_lead` | Score a person 0-100 against an ICP (from craft_icp). |
| `set_sender_profile` | Save the default sender profile (name, email, pitch, optional cta_url and bio). |

## local

**Local**, version 0.1.0.

Zero-key tools and free capability fallbacks that run on this machine: ffmpeg media tools and video upscaling, speech to text (parakeet-mlx, Hex, whisperX or whisper.cpp), Ollama chat, translation, embeddings and reranking, Kokoro speech, ComfyUI image generation and editing, Real-ESRGAN upscaling, rembg cutouts, Demucs stems, pdftotext, Tesseract and OCRmyPDF parsing, pandoc and LibreOffice conversion, and yt-dlp transcripts. Each backend is detected, never assumed.

Keys:

- `HF_TOKEN` (optional): Hugging Face token (whisperX speaker labels). Get one at https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens

Permissions:

- Local network: `127.0.0.1:8188`, `127.0.0.1:11434`, `127.0.0.1:8880`
- Runs programs: `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe`, `whisper-cli`, `whisper-cpp`, `parakeet-mlx`, `hex`, `whisperx`, `realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan`, `rembg`, `demucs`, `tesseract`, `ocrmypdf`, `pdftotext`, `pandoc`, `soffice`, `yt-dlp`
- Artifact library: full

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `local_audio_concat` | Join two or more library audio files end to end with local ffmpeg (for example per-turn speech into one podcast track). |
| `local_audio_mix` | Mix a voice track with background music or effects using local ffmpeg: presets ad, narration, podcast, trailer (or custom), intro/outro padding, fades, sidechain ducking under the voice, voice cleanup and loudness normalisation to -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP. |
| `local_chat` | Chat with a model running in local Ollama. |
| `local_comfy_run_workflow` | Run an arbitrary API-format ComfyUI node graph (Save (API Format) JSON) on your ComfyUI server, wait for it and save every output image, video or audio file to the library. |
| `local_comfy_status` | Check the local ComfyUI server: version, GPU devices, queue length and installed checkpoints. |
| `local_contact_sheet` | Lay out library images (or the first frame of videos) on one grid image (a contact sheet) with local ffmpeg. |
| `local_embed` | Compute text embeddings with a local Ollama embedding model (for example nomic-embed-text). |
| `local_generate_image` | Generate images from a text prompt with local ComfyUI using a built-in txt2img workflow and an installed checkpoint (no API key). |
| `local_media_convert` | Transcode, trim, scale, reframe (fixed 9:16, 16:9 or 1:1 outputs), extract audio, make a GIF or take a thumbnail from a library video/audio artifact, using local ffmpeg. |
| `local_media_probe` | Inspect a library artifact with ffprobe: container, duration, size, and per-stream codec, resolution, frame rate, sample rate and channels. |
| `local_ollama_models` | List the models installed in the local Ollama server (name, size, family, quantization). |
| `local_speak` | Turn text (up to 5000 characters) into speech with local Kokoro and save it as an audio artifact. |
| `local_status` | Detect which local backends work on this machine: ffmpeg/ffprobe, the speech engines (whisper.cpp with its models, parakeet-mlx, Hex, whisperX), Ollama (models), ComfyUI (checkpoints), Kokoro (voices) and the command-line tools behind the free capability fallbacks (Real-ESRGAN, rembg, Demucs, pdftotext, Tesseract, OCRmyPDF, pandoc, LibreOffice, yt-dlp). |
| `local_transcribe` | Transcribe a library audio or video artifact on this machine with parakeet-mlx (Apple silicon), whisper.cpp, Hex or whisperX, whichever is installed (or the one named by engine / the transcriptionEngine setting). |
| `local_video_burn_captions` | Burn SRT or WebVTT captions (an artifact, for example from local_transcribe) into a video artifact with local ffmpeg. |
| `local_video_concat` | Join two or more library videos end to end with local ffmpeg. |
| `local_video_mux_audio` | Put an audio artifact onto a video artifact with local ffmpeg: replace the video's audio or mix the two. |
| `local_voices` | List the voices offered by the local Kokoro-FastAPI server. |

## machines

**Machines**, version 0.1.0.

Register machines (SSH hosts today), run commands on them, move files between them and the artifact library, and update git checkouts on them.

Off by default. Switch it on in the dashboard under Packs.

Permissions:

- Runs programs: `ssh`
- Artifact library: full

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `machine_add` | Register an existing SSH host as a machine. |
| `machine_add_repo` | Register (or replace, by name) a git checkout on a machine for machine_update_repo: the folder path on the machine, an optional branch, and an optional post_update shell command run in that folder after the pull (e.g. |
| `machine_get_file` | Download a regular file from a registered machine into the artifact library and return the new artifact. |
| `machine_put_file` | Upload an artifact from the library to a path on a registered machine (overwrites). |
| `machine_remove` | Unregister a machine and the repos registered on it. |
| `machine_remove_repo` | Unregister a repo by name. |
| `machine_run` | Run a shell command on a registered machine over SSH and return stdout, stderr and the exit code. |
| `machine_status` | Connect to a registered machine and report whether it is reachable, the round-trip time and `uname -srm`. |
| `machine_update_repo` | Update a registered repo on its machine: cd into the folder, `git pull --ff-only` (on the registered branch if any), then run its post_update command. |
| `machines_list` | List the registered machines (name, provider, user@host:port, auth method) and the repos registered on them. |

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `google_directions` | Route between two addresses with the Google Routes API: distance, duration and turn-by-turn steps. |
| `google_geocode` | Turn an address or place name into coordinates with the Google Geocoding API. |
| `google_places_search` | Search places by text ("pizza in Lisbon", "Eiffel Tower") with Google Places Text Search. |
| `mapbox_directions` | Route through 2 to 25 points (longitude, latitude) with Mapbox Directions: distance, duration and turn-by-turn steps. |
| `mapbox_geocode` | Turn an address or place name into coordinates with Mapbox Geocoding v6. |

## media

**Media**, version 0.1.0.

Provider-neutral media, document, text and web tools: generate and edit images, video, speech, music and sound, transcribe, separate stems, clone voices, make 3D models, parse and convert documents, translate, embed, rerank, search and fetch the web. Each call goes to the best configured provider (local backends first, then paid APIs) and falls back on outages.

Permissions:

- Calls other tools: `cap:image.generate`, `cap:video.generate`, `cap:speech.generate`, `cap:music.generate`, `cap:audio.transcribe`, `cap:chat`, `cap:image.edit`, `cap:image.upscale`, `cap:image.remove_background`, `cap:video.upscale`, `cap:video.lipsync`, `cap:audio.separate_stems`, `cap:voice.clone`, `cap:sound.effect`, `cap:3d.generate`, `cap:document.parse`, `cap:document.convert`, `cap:text.translate`, `cap:text.embed`, `cap:text.rerank`, `cap:web.search`, `cap:web.fetch`, `cap:media.transcript`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | Send messages to a chat model through the best configured provider. |
| `clone_voice` | Create a reusable voice from library audio samples of one speaker. |
| `convert_document` | Convert a library document to another format (pdf, docx, html, md, ...) with the best configured provider (LibreOffice or pandoc locally). |
| `edit_image` | Edit a library image from a text instruction (change, add or remove things; optional mask and reference images) with the best configured provider. |
| `embed_text` | Turn texts into embedding vectors with the best configured provider. |
| `fetch_web` | Fetch a web page as clean Markdown (or text or HTML) with the best configured provider (a local browser, Jina or Firecrawl). |
| `generate_3d` | Generate a 3D model (GLB by default) from a text prompt, a library image, or both, with the best configured provider. |
| `generate_image` | Generate or edit images with the best configured provider. |
| `generate_music` | Generate music from a text prompt with the best configured provider. |
| `generate_sound_effect` | Generate a sound effect from a text description with the best configured provider. |
| `generate_speech` | Turn text into spoken audio with the best configured provider (voice and model are provider ids). |
| `generate_video` | Generate a short video clip with the best configured provider, optionally from a first and last frame (library image artifact ids). |
| `get_media_transcript` | Get the transcript of an online video or podcast by URL (YouTube and others) with the best configured provider: published captions when there are any, otherwise a transcription. |
| `lipsync_video` | Make the face in a library video (or image) speak a library audio track, with the best configured provider. |
| `list_media_providers` | List the providers behind the media tools: which are set up, their priority, models and cooldowns, per capability. |
| `parse_document` | Extract the text of a library PDF or image as Markdown or plain text (OCR for scans) with the best configured provider. |
| `remove_background` | Cut the subject out of a library image onto a transparent background (PNG) with the best configured provider. |
| `rerank_text` | Order documents by relevance to a query with the best configured provider. |
| `search_web` | Search the web with the best configured search provider (Exa, Tavily, Brave, Parallel, Firecrawl). |
| `separate_stems` | Split a library song into stems (vocals, drums, bass, other; or two_stems for vocals and instrumental) with the best configured provider. |
| `transcribe_audio` | Transcribe an audio or video library artifact to text, optionally with timestamps and speaker labels, with the best configured provider. |
| `translate_text` | Translate text into another language with the best configured provider (DeepL, a chat model, or a local Ollama model). |
| `upscale_image` | Upscale a library image 2x to 4x with the best configured provider (local Real-ESRGAN first when installed). |
| `upscale_video` | Upscale a library video 2x to 4x with the best configured provider (local ffmpeg resizes; AI providers restore detail). |

## memory

**Memory**, version 0.1.0.

Long-term semantic memory for agents: remember text with tags and metadata, recall it by meaning, forget it. Embeddings come from your text.embed provider; vectors are stored locally in SQLite (sqlite-vec, with a pure JS fallback).

Permissions:

- Calls other tools: `cap:text.embed`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `forget` | Delete memories. |
| `list_memories` | Page through the memories in a collection, newest first, optionally only those carrying every given tag. |
| `list_memory_collections` | List memory collections with their memory counts and the embedding provider, model and dimensions each is pinned to, plus the search mode in use (sqlite-vec index or brute-force JS fallback). |
| `recall` | Search long-term memory by meaning: returns the stored texts closest to `query` in a collection, best first, with a cosine similarity score (1 is identical). |
| `remember` | Store text in long-term semantic memory so it can be found later by meaning with recall. |

## mounts

**Remote MCP servers**, version 0.1.0.

Preconfigured remote MCP servers. Every one is off until you switch it on and set its key (or sign in, for the OAuth ones). Their tools appear as <prefix>__<tool>; what they return is untrusted data.

Keys:

- `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` (optional): Firecrawl API key. Get one at https://docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server
- `EXA_API_KEY` (optional): Exa API key. Get one at https://dashboard.exa.ai/api-keys
- `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` (optional): Browserbase API key. Get one at https://www.browserbase.com/overview
- `TAVILY_API_KEY` (optional): Tavily API key. Get one at https://app.tavily.com
- `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` (optional): Perplexity API key. Get one at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/integrations/mcp-server
- `JINA_API_KEY` (optional): Jina AI API key. Get one at https://jina.ai
- `APIFY_TOKEN` (optional): Apify API token. Get one at https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/mcp
- `GITHUB_MCP_PAT` (optional): GitHub personal access token. Get one at https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new
- `LINEAR_API_KEY` (optional): Linear API key. Get one at https://linear.app/docs/mcp
- `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` (optional): Context7 API key. Get one at https://context7.com/dashboard
- `RUNPOD_API_KEY` (optional): Runpod API key. Get one at https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/mcp-servers
- `HF_TOKEN` (optional): Hugging Face token. Get one at https://huggingface.co/settings/mcp

Mounted servers (each off until switched on): `firecrawl`, `exa`, `browserbase`, `tavily`, `perplexity`, `jina`, `apify`, `github`, `linear`, `context7`, `runpod`, `huggingface`, `deepwiki`, `sentry`, `cloudflare-browser`, `notion`, `context-dev`, `linear-oauth`, `atlassian`, `stripe`, `cloudflare`, `composio`, `pipedream`, `zapier`

## workflows

**Workflows**, version 0.1.0.

Ready-made multi-step workflows on top of the media, local, web and ElevenLabs tools: issue triage, short and launch videos, narrated ads, a brand kit from a URL, dubbing and podcast production. Each runs as a job; call it with dry_run: true first to see the steps, what is missing and the most paid calls it can make.

Permissions:

- Artifact library: write
- Calls other tools: `chat`, `generate_image`, `generate_video`, `generate_speech`, `generate_music`, `transcribe_audio`, `local_audio_mix`, `local_audio_concat`, `local_video_concat`, `local_video_mux_audio`, `local_video_burn_captions`, `local_transcribe`, `firecrawl_scrape`, `screenshot_url`, `elevenlabs_dub`

Workflows: `brand_kit_from_url`, `dub_localize`, `issue_triage`, `podcast_produce`, `video_launch_film_16x9`, `video_narrated_ad`, `video_short_9x16`

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `wf_brand_kit_from_url` | A brand kit from a website: a screenshot (local headless browser) and the page text (Firecrawl, when set up) are read side by side, a model drafts the kit (name, tagline, voice, colors, fonts, logo direction) and it is saved to the library as JSON and as a Markdown brand sheet. |
| `wf_dub_localize` | Localize a video or audio file into 1 to 5 languages. |
| `wf_issue_triage` | Triage one bug report or feature request: type, severity, suggested labels and components, missing information, next steps and a draft reply. |
| `wf_podcast_produce` | A podcast episode from a topic and notes: a model writes the script (one host, or a two-host conversation) and the show notes, text-to-speech reads it, and the show notes are saved as a Markdown document. |
| `wf_video_launch_film_16x9` | A 16:9 product launch film in five beats (hook, problem, solution, proof, call to action): a model writes the beats from your product notes (and the product page, when you give a URL and Firecrawl is set up), each beat becomes a generated clip, the clips are joined and a voice-over is laid on top. |
| `wf_video_narrated_ad` | A narrated ad, script first: a model writes 2 to 6 script lines, each with the visual it plays over; one voice reads the whole script, each visual becomes a generated clip in the aspect you pick, and the clips are joined under the voice. |
| `wf_video_short_9x16` | A 9:16 short (Reels, Shorts, TikTok) from a topic: a model plans 2 to 8 shots with narration, each shot is generated as a video clip, the clips are joined, a voice-over reads the narration and captions are burned in locally. |

## x402

**x402 payments**, version 0.1.0.

Pay per call for x402 paid APIs in USDC from a small wallet you dedicate to it, with a person's approval every time and hard per-call and daily limits (x402_quote, x402_fetch, x402_wallet).

Off by default. Switch it on in the dashboard under Packs.

Keys:

- `X402_PRIVATE_KEY` (optional): x402 wallet private key (a small, dedicated wallet). Get one at https://docs.x402.org

Permissions:

- Network: `*`
- Artifact library: write

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `x402_fetch` | Fetch an x402 paid URL and pay for it in USDC from the pack's wallet: sends the request, and when it answers 402 picks the cheapest option this pack can pay (exact scheme, USDC on an allowed network) that costs at most max_usd and fits the pack's per-call and 24-hour limits, signs the payment and sends the request again with it. |
| `x402_quote` | Ask an x402 paid URL what it costs, without paying: sends a read-only GET (or HEAD) with no payment and, when it answers 402 Payment Required, lists each payment option with its price in USD, network, recipient and whether this pack could pay it (and why not). |
| `x402_wallet` | Show the x402 wallet: its address (never the key), the networks and limits in force, what was paid in the last 24 hours and the most recent payments. |
